brief.summary: Stocks were lower early, with S&P and Nasdaq futures down modestly and a fourth straight decline in play, though futures pared losses as crude pulled back. Front-end and long-end Treasury yields rose to fresh highs, with 10-year near 4.81% and 30-year around 5.29%, while oil stayed elevated near $95 Brent on US-Iran escalation. The Fed narrative turned more hawkish: about 70% odds of a September hike are priced, and officials including Barr sounded open to raising rates. Credit spreads were mostly tight but tech/AI issuance showed some widening. The dominant narrative is a supply-shock, hawkish-Fed, fiscal-risk backdrop; tone is risk-off, though AI earnings strength keeps dip-buying alive.
